answer.why_different: The generated document omits the entire callback structure at the callback location. This is a structural omission, not a changed value or a callback address declared at another location.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification explicitly maps notifyMOICreation to an HTTP POST at the notification target, and defines NotifyMoiCreation as the notification type. It also specifies a 204 success response with no body and an ErrorResponse for failures.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 defines callbacks as operations initiated by the API provider, with a runtime-expression key identifying the callback URL. The official callback uses the request body's notificationRecipientAddress as that expression and defines the POST request and responses accordingly.
answer.clearer_why: The official version exposes the notification callback, its target expression, payload schema, and expected responses. The generated version provides no callback definition, so a reader cannot determine that notifyMOICreation notifications are supported or how they are delivered.

evidence.title: Examples
evidence.text:
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
